Django's model `FilePathField` already accepts a callable `path`. `deconstruct()` stores `self.path` as given, so migrations keep the callable instead of the resolved path. `formfield()` calls it when it is callable, with `self.path() if callable(self.path) else self.path`. That call is the line I'm submitting.

The DurationField "invalid" error message in `django/db/models/fields/__init__.py` shows the wrong format string, `[DD] [[HH:]MM:]ss[.uuuuuu]`. It should be `[DD] [[[HH:]MM:]ss[.uuuuuu]` with the brackets fixed to `[DD] [[HH:]MM:]ss[.uuuuuu]` → `[DD] [[[HH:]MM:]ss[.uuuuuu]`. Seconds are mandatory, minutes are optional, and hours are optional only when minutes are given. The correct string is `[DD] [[[HH:]MM:]ss[.uuuuuu]`. I did not edit the file. The message is at line 1847. The "default help text" suggestion in the report is a separate change.
HttpResponse (django/http/response.py, HttpResponseBase.make_bytes) handles memoryview by converting it with bytes(value), and the content setter excludes memoryview from the iterator branch.

The fix is in Collector.delete() in django/db/models/deletion.py. In the single-object fast-delete path, `setattr(instance, model._meta.pk.attname, None)` clears the instance's primary key after the delete query runs. The placeholder [name] is most likely "PK" (and "delete" for the method name, "Collector.delete" for the reference). The ticket's line numbers (276-281) are from an older version, so the code has moved to line 456.

The failure comes from update_proxy_model_permissions in auth migration 0011_update_proxy_permissions. It moves proxy-model permissions to the proxy's ContentType with an update(). When a model was recreated as a proxy, permissions with those codenames already exist for the proxy's content type, so the update hits the unique (content_type_id, codename) constraint. In this version of the file the update is wrapped in a transaction.atomic block that catches IntegrityError and prints a warning, so the migration no longer crashes. I did not run anything to confirm this.

The autoreloader now handles the `__main__` module (usually manage.py) as a special case in `iter_modules_and_files`. That module often has no `__spec__`, so the reloader would skip it and never watch it. The code falls back to `module.__file__` for `__main__` and `__mp_main__`, so edits to manage.py trigger a reload. I found this by reading the code. I didn't run anything.

The autoreloader handles this in `iter_modules_and_files` in `django/utils/autoreload.py`. It catches the `ValueError` ("embedded null byte") raised by `path.exists()`. A comment there says network filesystems may return null bytes in file paths. It logs the error at debug level and skips that path. The `sys_path_directories` function, around line 211, calls `path.exists()` with no such guard.

Django already handles this in `LazySettings.__getattr__`. For `MEDIA_URL` and `STATIC_URL`, it calls `_add_script_prefix`. That method prepends `get_script_prefix()` (the SCRIPT_NAME) to relative values. It leaves absolute paths and URLs alone, because it skips values that start with `http://`, `https://` or `/`. Static and media URLs therefore pick up the sub-path prefix when the setting is read.

I didn't open the `{% static %}` tag code or the storage classes, so I haven't confirmed that they pick up this prefix.

The check is in Field._check_choices in django/db/models/fields/__init__.py. It returns error fields.E009, "'max_length' is too small to fit the longest value in 'choices'", when the longest choice value is longer than max_length.

The check is check_all_models in django/core/checks/model_checks.py: duplicate db_table across models raises models.E028 ("db_table '%s' is used by multiple models"). When settings.DATABASE_ROUTERS is configured, it is downgraded to a warning (models.W035) with a hint to verify the models are routed to separate databases.

The placeholders look like DEBUG (when DEBUG is True) and to_python (the converter method). The code that handles this is technical_404_response in django/views/debug.py. When the Http404 carries no "tried" data, as with a converter's to_python, it falls back to `request.resolver_match.tried if request.resolver_match else None`. That fallback is on line 619. I did not run anything to reproduce the plain-text error. The match fails because RoutePattern.match in django/urls/resolvers.py:314 only catches ValueError from converter.to_python.

Django's EnumSerializer.serialize in django/db/migrations/serializer.py already writes enum members by name, as `module.EnumClass['NAME']`. The f-string at line 144 does this with `item.name!r`. Flag enums are decomposed into members and joined with " | ".

The check is in `parse_http_date` in `corpus/django/utils/http.py`, and the code there already compares against the current year instead of using a hard-coded 0-69 / 70-99 split. For a two-digit year, it takes the current year and its century. If the parsed year is more than 50 above the current two-digit year, it moves the date back one century. Otherwise it uses the current century. Line 121 is the comparison that does this: `if year - (current_year % 100) > 50:`.
The `__isnull` lookup. `IsNull.as_sql` raises `ValueError` ("The QuerySet value for an isnull lookup must be True or False.") when the right-hand side isn't a `bool`.

The fix is `Choices.__str__` in `corpus/django/db/models/enums.py`. It returns `str(self.value)`, so a Choices enum member set as a model instance attribute converts to its plain value instead of `ClassName.MEMBER`. I found it by reading the file and did not run the report's test.

The fix is in `generate_altered_fields()` in the migration autodetector. For a ForeignKey, it checks whether the target field (`to_field`) was renamed. If it was, it points the new field's `remote_field.model` and `remote_field.field_name` back at the old values. Both are reset together because `ForeignKey.deconstruct()` decides whether to include `to_field` based on both. The line I'm submitting is the `field_name` assignment, which is the part that handles the renamed `to_field`.

`ProjectState.rename_field()` in `django/db/migrations/state.py` (lines 321-336) also updates `to_field` references to the new name. I picked the autodetector as the main fix because it is where the stale `to_field` value is handled when migrations are generated. I didn't run any code to confirm this.

The issue is overriding the auto-generated get_FOO_display() method on models with choices. Field.contribute_to_class() now only sets get_FOO_display if it isn't already in cls.__dict__, so an explicit override on the class is kept.
Field.deconstruct() builds the path from the class's __qualname__ instead of __name__. That makes an inner class serialize as Outer.Inner rather than as a top-level class.

SQLite test_db_signature(): for on-disk test databases it appends the test database name to the signature, so each alias with a distinct TEST NAME gets its own database. This is the `else` branch, `sig.append(test_database_name)`.

The code that preserves the inner query's GROUP BY is the `if self.group_by is True:` block in `Query.set_values` in `corpus/django/db/models/sql/query.py`. I did not confirm this by running the example, and I am not certain it is the exact line the question wants.

That block expands the group-by to the model's concrete fields and calls `set_group_by(allow_aliases=False)` before the select clause is cleared. The `elif self.group_by:` branch just below it resolves group-by references to annotations that are no longer selected.

The repo already seems to contain the fix. `Exact.get_prep_lookup` (`lookups.py:332`) and `In.get_prep_lookup` (`lookups.py:457`) only clear the select clause and add `pk` when `has_select_fields` is false. `set_values` sets `has_select_fields = True` at line 2387. Together these should stop the `id=a[:1]` filter from replacing the inner query's `email` with `id`.

RegexPattern.match in django/urls/resolvers.py filters out named groups that didn't participate in the match (value None). Optional named groups are therefore not passed as kwargs, and the view's default (format='html') applies. The filtering line is `kwargs = {k: v for k, v in kwargs.items() if v is not None}`.

The method is Model.get_FOO_display(), set up in Field.contribute_to_class(). The check `"get_%s_display" % self.name not in cls.__dict__` only looks at the class's own `__dict__`. Because of that, a child model that overrides the choices gets its own get_FOO_display bound to the child's field. Earlier code checked `hasattr(cls, ...)`, which found the inherited method and skipped this step, so the parent's choices were used. That is why "C" came back as "C". This code already has the fix.

The bug is in `BaseDatabaseCreation.deserialize_db_from_string()`, which is the method the report calls `deserialize_db_from_string`. It used to deserialize and save objects without a transaction. In find_ordering_name (django/db/models/sql/compiler.py), the condition that expands a relation's default ordering now includes `name != "pk"`. The "-pk" ordering is therefore no longer replaced by the related model's Meta.ordering. That is how the "-pk" ordering gets handled for inherited models. The `pk` clause is at line 1055.

The special case for JSONField belongs in `display_for_field()` in `django/contrib/admin/utils.py`. The branch `elif isinstance(field, models.JSONField) and value:` is already there. SafeExceptionReporterFilter.cleanse_setting in corpus/django/views/debug.py. It now recurses into lists and tuples as well as dicts, which is what the report asks for. Other iterables, such as sets, are still returned as-is. I didn't run it.

The hint in the E334/E335 checks (ManyToManyField intermediary model with ambiguous foreign keys) is at related.py:1550. In this copy it already reads 'use ManyToManyField("%s", through="%s")', with no ForeignKey or symmetrical=False. The identical E335 hint is at line 1571.

The crash comes from `_delete_composed_index` in `corpus/django/db/backends/base/schema.py`. It looks up constraints on the index_together columns, and it raises `ValueError("Found wrong number (%s) of constraints for %s(%s)")` when it finds anything other than exactly one. I didn't reproduce the crash.

The "column reference "status" is ambiguous" error most likely comes from `Query.set_group_by`. When aliases are allowed and the annotation has no aggregate, it adds `Ref(alias, annotation)` to GROUP BY. That makes the SQL group by the bare alias "status", which clashes with the joined table's own "status" column. Django 2.2 grouped by the full subquery expression instead. I didn't confirm this against the upstream fix or a reproduction, so it is my best reading of the code rather than a verified result.

The result comes from `Collector.delete()` in `django/db/models/deletion.py`, which `QuerySet.delete()` calls. It builds the `(total, per-model dict)` tuple with a `Counter` and returns it at line 522. The code already handles the zero case. The fast-delete loop (line 473) and the instance-delete loop (line 507) both do `if count:` before adding to the counter, so a model with zero deleted objects never gets a key. That makes both cases return `(0, {})`. I did not run it.

The one other return is the single-instance fast path at line 457. It always returns `{label: count}`, but `count` can't be zero there because exactly one instance is being deleted.
The [name] is distinct(). QuerySet.distinct() calls self._not_support_combined_queries("distinct"), which raises NotSupportedError when the queryset is a union or other combined query.

The missing method is `get_response_async`. It was added to `StaticFilesHandlerMixin`, so `ASGIStaticFilesHandler` inherits it. It serves the file through `sync_to_async(self.serve)` and turns `Http404` into a response with `response_for_exception`.

The check is already in `Model._check_constraints`. It collects the fields of every UniqueConstraint (`fields` and `include`), plus fields referenced by conditions and expressions. It then passes them to `cls._check_local_fields(fields, "constraints")`. That call raises models.E012 for nonexistent fields. The reusable helper is `_check_local_fields` at base.py:2079.

The fix is already in `slugify()` in `corpus/django/utils/text.py`. Its last line, `return re.sub(r"[-\s]+", "-", value).strip("-_")`, strips leading and trailing dashes and underscores. That makes `slugify("this is a test ---")` return `this-is-a-test`. I haven't run it. I read the code and didn't test it.

Query.check_filterable in django/db/models/sql/query.py raises NotSupportedError ("<ClassName> is disallowed in the filter clause."). It does this when the value passed to the filter has `resolve_expression` and its `filterable` attribute is False. A model instance that has a field named `filterable=False` trips this check.

The fix is in Query.set_empty(). It adds a NothingNode to the query's where clause and then calls set_empty() on each query in combined_queries. This makes QuerySet.none() empty a union/combined queryset instead of returning all results.

The ordering code in `find_ordering_name` (django/db/models/sql/compiler.py) appends the related model's default `Meta.ordering` whenever the ordered field is a relation. The fix for this ticket is the condition `getattr(field, "attname", None) != pieces[-1]` at line 1054. With it, ordering by `root_id` (the field's attname) is treated as ordering by the raw column. It no longer adds the extra self-join or applies the related model's default ordering. I found this by reading the code; I didn't run the queryset from the ticket.

ValidationError.__eq__ in django/core/exceptions.py. It returns NotImplemented for non-ValidationError objects. Otherwise it compares hash(self) == hash(other), and the order-independent comparison is handled in __hash__ just below it.
Add `comments` support: a `comments` argument to `SyndicationFeed.add_item()` in django/utils/feedgenerator.py, which the syndication view passes via `item_comments`.

The fix is in `apply_limit_choices_to_to_formfield` in `django/forms/models.py`. It wraps the `limit_choices_to` Q object in an `Exists()` subquery instead of joining, so a join can no longer produce duplicate options. The code comment on that line reads "Use Exists() to avoid potential duplicates." I read the code but did not run the regression test.

SessionBase.decode in corpus/django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py handles invalid session data. It catches signing.BadSignature, logs "Session data corrupted", and returns {}. A generic `except Exception` at line 109 catches any other decoding error, such as "Incorrect padding", and also returns an empty session. I didn't find a legacy decode path in this code. The model class is added to the app_list context via `"model": model` in the model_dict built by `AdminSite._build_app_dict` (the method the ticket also asks to make public, as `build_app_dict`). It is used by both the index and app_index views.

Field.__eq__ in corpus/django/db/models/fields/__init__.py now compares both creation_counter and the field's model, so fields from different models are unequal. __lt__ (line 669) orders by creation_counter first and uses the model only to break ties. __hash__ (line 689) still hashes only creation_counter. That is consistent with __eq__, but it does not include the model.

The crash comes from `serialize_db_to_string()` in `corpus/django/db/backends/base/creation.py`. With `"TEST": {"MIGRATE": False}`, `create_test_db` sets `MIGRATION_MODULES` to `None` for every app, so migrate only syncdbs the tables. The serializer then queries models that have no table. The guard `app_config.label in loader.migrated_apps` on line 128 is what skips those apps. I did not run anything, and I'm assuming that guard is the fix for this ticket rather than confirming it against the traceback.

The question reads as the Django ticket "AddIndex with order_with_respect_to crash when _order is included in indexes". The autodetector handles this in `generate_created_models`. It emits `AlterOrderWithRespectTo`, which creates the `_order` field, before the `AddIndex` operations. The `if order_with_respect_to:` block at line 702 comes first. The `AddIndex` loop at line 718 comes after it. For models that already exist, `generate_altered_order_with_respect_to()` runs at line 198, before `generate_added_indexes()` at line 201. I didn't run a migration to reproduce the crash. This is the code that fixes the ordering.

Query.resolve_lookup_value in django/db/models/sql/query.py. It rebuilt the tuple with type_(values), passing a generator. That fails for named tuples. The fix is the namedtuple branch at lines 1228-1229, which calls type_(*values).

The fix is in PasswordResetTokenGenerator._make_hash_value in django/contrib/auth/tokens.py. It appends the user's email to the hash value, read through user.get_email_field_name() and falling back to "" if the user has no email. Changing the email therefore invalidates any outstanding reset tokens.

The -c crash comes from `exec(options["command"], globals())` in `handle()` in shell.py. It passes the module's globals. Passing a fresh empty dict instead, `exec(options["command"], {})`, fixes it. The stdin branch at line 127 has the same problem.

InlineModelAdmin.__init__ in django/contrib/admin/options.py derives verbose_name_plural from the inline's verbose_name (format_lazy("{}s", self.verbose_name)) when verbose_name_plural isn't set but verbose_name is.
ManagementUtility.execute creates the CommandParser for --settings/--pythonpath; the fix is passing prog=self.prog_name (already-computed from argv) instead of defaulting to sys.argv[0].

KeyTransformIsNull in django/db/models/fields/json.py implements key__isnull=True/False. The fix is its as_oracle and as_sqlite methods, which use HasKeyOrArrayIndex (JSON_TYPE ... IS NULL on SQLite). That way isnull=True matches only rows that lack the key, not rows where the key's value is JSON null.

models.W042 is the warning raised. `Model._check_default_pk` in django/db/models/base.py emits it, and it appears when you run `manage.py check` or `migrate`. The check now skips models whose pk is an inherited parent_link OneToOneField, because the parent model is checked instead.

ModelChoiceField's default "invalid_choice" error message (django/forms/models.py) lacks the %(value)s placeholder, so the invalid value isn't shown. The fix is to put the value in the message, e.g. "Select a valid choice. %(value)s is not one of the available choices.". `to_python` already passes params={"value": value}.

Signal.send_robust() now logs exceptions raised by receivers. Its except clauses call `self._log_robust_failure(receiver, err)`, which does `logger.error("Error calling %s in Signal.send_robust() (%s)", ..., exc_info=err)`. The logger.error call is in `_log_robust_failure`.

In Model._prepare_related_fields_for_save (django/db/models/base.py), the check `elif getattr(self, field.attname) in field.empty_values:` re-syncs the FK from the related object when the parent's FK value is empty (e.g. "" for a CharField pk). The bug was that it only handled None (auto pk), so a non-numeric pk set after assignment stayed as "".

Q._combine raises TypeError(other) when the other operand is not Q-like (no truthy `conditional` attribute). That is what Q(...) & Exists(...) hits. Exists & Q(...) works because Combinable.__and__ wraps both operands in Q.

Q._combine in django/db/models/query_utils.py: it must use a shallow copy (other.copy() / self.copy()) instead of copy.deepcopy when one side of the | operand is empty, so non-pickleable values in Q children don't get deep-copied (Node.__copy__ in utils/tree.py).

The `AutoFieldMeta._subclasses` property returns `(BigAutoField, SmallAutoField)`. `AutoFieldMeta.__subclasscheck__` calls `issubclass(subclass, self._subclasses)`, and this fails for subclasses of BigAutoField and SmallAutoField when `DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD` points at one. The check should also accept subclasses of those classes. I did not run this or test a change.

ResolverMatch.__init__() in corpus/django/urls/resolvers.py doesn't unwrap functools.partial objects. It computes `_func_path` from `func` as-is, so the repr falls back to `repr(self.func)` at line 79 and shows the partial's raw `func` argument. The fix is to unwrap partials at the start of the `func` handling, before the `view_class` check at line 63. That means taking `func.func` and merging the partial's pre-supplied args and keywords. I didn't edit the file.

The bug was in TemplateCommand.handle (django/core/management/templates.py). It called validate_name(os.path.basename(target), "directory"). A trailing slash makes basename return an empty string, which fails validation. In this corpus the code is already fixed. It takes the basename of top_dir, which is os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(target)), and abspath strips the trailing slash.

BoundWidget.id_for_label returns self.data["attrs"].get("id"), so it uses the id set by ChoiceWidget.options. The old code ignored that id and rebuilt it from the auto_id format string. The code here already has the fix.

ReadOnlyPasswordHashWidget.id_for_label returns None, so the label gets no 'for' attribute. The widget only renders text and has no labelable element. BoundField.label_tag in django/forms/boundfield.py only adds 'for' when id_for_label is truthy (lines 189-192), so returning None here drops it.

The fix is in TypeSerializer.serialize in django/db/migrations/serializer.py. Its special case for `models.Model` returns the string "models.Model" together with the import "from django.db import models". Without that import entry, a model whose base class is `models.Model` (for example a mixin) is written into the migration as `models.Model` with no `models` import, which gives "name 'models' is not defined". In this corpus the import is already present on that line.

BaseFormSet.full_clean() in django/forms/formsets.py builds `_non_form_errors` with `error_class="nonform"`. It does this at line 400 for the initial empty error list. It does it again at lines 456-459 when a ValidationError is caught. Forms already do the same with "nonfield" in forms.py:254.

The check is in ManyToManyField's warning checks. It adds warning fields.W345 ("related_name has no effect on ManyToManyField with a symmetrical relationship, e.g. to "self"") when `self.remote_field.symmetrical and self._related_name`. It is a warning, not an error.
The missing call is make_hashable(self.through_fields) in ManyToManyRel.identity. It is already present in this corpus, so no fix is needed there.

Query.add_deferred_loading in django/db/models/sql/query.py: when deferred_loading is in "only" mode (defer=False), the else branch computes existing.difference(field_names); if nothing remains it calls clear_deferred_loading() (and defers any leftover new names), so only("name").defer("name") selects just id instead of all fields.

The fix for method_decorator is in `_multi_decorate`. It builds `bound_method = wraps(method)(partial(method.__get__(self, type(self))))`. `wraps(method)` copies the wrapper assignments, such as `__name__`, onto the otherwise bare `partial` object before the decorators see it.

The bug is in `AdminReadonlyField.get_admin_url` in `django/contrib/admin/helpers.py`. It builds the link with `reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])`, which always resolves under the default `admin` site. In this corpus the fix is already applied: the `reverse()` call passes `current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name` (line 255), so the link uses the custom Admin Site's name. I read the code but did not run the tests.
The unhashable type is ModelChoiceIteratorValue (django/forms/models.py). The fix is the `__hash__` method, which returns hash(self.value), so the class is hashable.

The ticket is about MultiWidget.id_for_label in django/forms/widgets.py. It originally returned f'{id_}_0', which put a "for" attribute on the label. The ticket proposes removing the method. In this code it is the version that returns "", so no "for" is rendered.

The fix belongs in RenameModel.database_forwards. It should return early when old_model._meta.db_table equals new_model._meta.db_table. At the moment the method only skips the main table rename, because alter_db_table returns early for equal names. It then still runs alter_field on every related field and _alter_many_to_many on the M2M fields. Those calls drop and recreate the foreign key constraints on Postgres and rebuild the table on SQLite. I didn't change or run any code.

The question is garbled. I read it as the Django ticket "URLField throws ValueError instead of ValidationError on clean". The fix is already in `forms.URLField.to_python`. Its `split_url` helper catches the `ValueError` that `urlsplit` raises on malformed URLs and re-raises it as `ValidationError(self.error_messages["invalid"], code="invalid")`. I read the code but did not run it or the example from the ticket.

The crash was fixed in `NegatedExpression.as_sql` in django/db/models/expressions.py. It now catches `EmptyResultSet`, which `~Q(pk__in=[])` raises. When that happens it compiles to a true value: `Value(True)`, or `"1=1"` on backends that can't use a boolean expression in SELECT. That is correct because the negation of an empty result set matches everything.

The crash comes from `Col.relabeled_clone`. SQLite's `_remake_table` renames table references in the constraint's expressions through `Expressions.rename_table_references`, which calls `relabeled_clone`. `Col` objects built with `alias_cols=False` have `alias = None`. Relabelling them used to give them a table alias, so they rendered as `"table"."column"`. SQLite rejects the "." operator in index expressions. The guard `if self.alias is None: return self` keeps such columns unqualified. I found this guard already in the corpus code at the line below. I did not run a reproduction.

MigrationRecorder.ensure_schema creates the django_migrations table on any connection, without consulting the db router's allow_migrate. It only checks has_table(), then calls create_model. record_applied and applied_migrations, which rely on it, have the same problem.

Subquery.as_sql() produced invalid SQL because it strips the first and last characters (`subquery_sql[1:-1]`) assuming the query is wrapped in brackets, which only happens when query.subquery = True. The fix is to set `self.query.subquery = True` in the Subquery constructor (`__init__`), which the code now does.

The blank [name] is `extra_tags`. The encoder in MessageEncoder.default now checks `obj.extra_tags is not None` instead of its truthiness, so an empty string `""` is serialised and restored as `""` rather than `None`. I found this fix already in the code and did not change anything. I only read cookie.py and did not run the replication.

The cause is in `template_changed` in `django/template/autoreload.py`. After BASE_DIR is added to `TEMPLATES[0]['DIRS']`, it becomes a watched template directory, and every file under it counts as a template change. `template_changed` then returns True, which tells the autoreloader the change was handled, so it skips the restart. That is why saving a `.py` file no longer restarts the server. The guard that fixes this is `if file_path.suffix == ".py": return` at line 49, with the `return` at line 50. It lets Python files fall through to the normal restart. I read the file but didn't run the repro.
SimpleLazyObject didn't implement __radd__ (the issue is about the missing __radd__ magic method; lazy-object-proxy has it). The fix is a proxied __radd__ that returns `other + self`.

RenameIndex.database_backwards in django/db/migrations/operations/models.py returns early as a no-op when old_fields is set (unnamed index). It never restores the old auto-generated name. Re-applying the rename then fails because the index with the new name already exists.

BaseCommand.create_parser now does kwargs.setdefault("formatter_class", DjangoHelpFormatter). A command can pass its own formatter_class, for example one that keeps newlines in the help text, and it won't be overridden.

The empty-string handling is in get_conditional_response in django/utils/cache.py. Line 176 is `if_modified_since = if_modified_since and parse_http_date_safe(if_modified_since)`. An empty header is falsy, so it short-circuits and is never parsed. A non-empty invalid value goes through the "safe" parser, which returns None instead of raising. That leaves the header ignored in both cases.

I found this by reading the code. I didn't run anything or check commit d6aff369ad3, so I can't confirm this is the line that commit changed.

The other place that reads the header is `was_modified_since` in django/views/static.py (lines 102-121). It catches the ValueError that `parse_http_date("")` raises and returns True, so an empty header doesn't raise there either.
django.utils.html.json_script() — it now takes an `encoder=None` parameter, which falls back to DjangoJSONEncoder when unset.

When a field changes between a concrete field (ForeignKey) and a ManyToManyField, the autodetector in `generate_altered_fields` can't emit an AlterField. It falls back to `_generate_removed_field` followed by `_generate_added_field`. `_generate_removed_field` adds the RemoveField with a dependency on the `foo_together_change` operation (`(app_label, model_name, field_name, "foo_together_change")`, line 1094). That dependency makes the `AlterUniqueTogether` that drops the unique_together run before the RemoveField. So a single migration handles both changes. The fallback call that does this is at line 1215. I only read the code and didn't run the reporter's project, so I haven't reproduced the error.
check_for_template_tags_with_the_same_name (the templates.E003 check) — the title is "check_for_template_tags_with_the_same_name with libraries in TEMPLATES"

inspectdb already generates related_name for relations to a model that an earlier field in the same table already used. The code is in the inspectdb command. It sets extra_params["related_name"] = "<model_name lowercased>_<att_name>_set" when rel_to is already in used_relations, and then adds rel_to to used_relations.

In PostgreSQL's DatabaseClient.settings_to_cmd_args_env, the extra parameters are added with args.extend(parameters) before the dbname is appended with args += [dbname]. This puts the database name last, as psql expects.

EnumSerializer.serialize in django/db/migrations/serializer.py handles Flag enums by decomposing the value into its member names (list(self.value) on PY311+, enum._decompose otherwise) and joining the `Class[name]` expressions with " | ".

The crash is already fixed in this codebase. The old `opts = cur_model._meta` line no longer exists. Related models are now resolved through their concrete model, so proxy models work. For `only()` this is `related_model = field.remote_field.model._meta.concrete_model`, followed by `related_model._meta` being passed to `_get_only_select_mask`. The `defer()` path does the same at line 746.

FormSet.empty_form in django/forms/formsets.py: form_kwargs for empty_form merges get_form_kwargs(None) first and then forces "empty_permitted": True (and use_required_attribute False), so a user-supplied empty_permitted in form_kwargs is ignored for empty_form instead of raising a duplicate-keyword TypeError.

The fix belongs in the `ManagementForm` class in `django/forms/formsets.py`. The upstream fix, as I remember it, is to give that class its own `template_name = "django/forms/div.html"` so it never triggers the default-template deprecation warning. It only renders hidden inputs, so the template makes no difference to the output. This corpus has no such warning any more: the 5.0-era code has no `RemovedInDjango50Warning` and no `template_name` on `ManagementForm`. The only form-renderer warnings left are for `DjangoDivFormRenderer` and `Jinja2DivFormRenderer`. I didn't find the warning-raising code itself. The line below points at the class where the fix would go.

The fix is already in the code. UserChangeForm.__init__ formats the password field's help text with `f"../../{self.instance.pk}/password/"` instead of the hard-coded `"../password/"`. The link now uses the instance's pk, so it works when the user is opened through a `to_field` such as `uuid`.

Model Field.formfield() sets show_hidden_initial=True for callable defaults. This renders the hidden "initial-..." input that triggers the bug. The `[name]=False` workaround in the report is `show_hidden_initial=False`.

The `str_number[0] == "-"` check in `format()` in django/utils/numberformat.py raises "string index out of range" when the number is null. `str(number)` is then an empty string, so indexing `[0]` fails.
ValueError is raised (max() of an empty sequence); the fix is changing `except TypeError:` to `except (TypeError, ValueError):` in get_latest_lastmod.

FileBasedCache.has_key in django/core/cache/backends/filebased.py. The race was between the os.path.exists() check and open(). In this code it is already handled: it opens the file directly and catches FileNotFoundError, returning False.

The fix is in `create_permissions`. It looks up content types with `ContentType.objects.db_manager(using).get_for_model(klass, for_concrete_model=False)`, so the lookup uses the database passed to migrate instead of going through the router. The original bug was an unscoped `ContentType.objects.get_for_model` call at this spot, which is what produced the extra router read.

The question is about the "show_save_as_new" tag in the admin's `submit_row` (corpus/django/contrib/admin/templatetags/admin_modify.py). "Save as new" is an add operation, so it should also require `has_add_permission`. In this code that check is already present: `show_save_as_new` is `not is_popup and has_add_permission and change and save_as`.

AlterField.reduce in django/db/migrations/operations/fields.py is where the optimizer logic lives. Its isinstance check, `isinstance(operation, (AlterField, RemoveField)) and self.is_same_field_operation(operation)`, returns `[operation]`. That makes consecutive AlterField operations on the same field reduce to the last one. The fix for this issue is already in the code: AlterField is in that tuple, next to RemoveField.

Multi-level FilteredRelation with select_related() sets the wrong related object because the filtered-relation klass_info in get_related_selections always installs a reverse local_setter. For a multi-join filtered relation (len(joins) > 2), that setter assigns the object to the wrong parent. The code handles this by using partial(local_setter, final_field) only when len(joins) <= 2, and local_setter_noop otherwise. I found this by reading the code. I didn't run the test case.

The filter is `join` (autoescape is `off`). In `join` in django/template/defaultfilters.py, the joining string is escaped only when `autoescape` is true (`conditional_escape(arg)`). When `autoescape` is off, the `else` branch does `arg.join(value)`, so neither the items nor the joining string are escaped.

The list_display item check in `_check_list_display_item` (corpus/django/contrib/admin/checks.py) is where this case is handled. It raises E108 only when the name is not a model field and not an attribute. A reverse relation such as "choice" resolves through `get_field()`, so it never reaches E108. The code here already adds a check at lines 933-936 that reports it as admin.E109 ("must not be a many-to-many field or a reverse foreign key"). I did not run this or check the repro, so I am not certain this is the intended fix location.

The squash optimizer handles this in `CreateModel.reduce`. When it meets a `RenameIndex` that has `old_fields`, it removes those fields from the model's `index_together` option. It then adds a `models.Index(fields=operation.old_fields, name=operation.new_name)` to `indexes`. The squashed `CreateModel` therefore no longer contains `index_together`, so the deprecation warning goes away. The branch starts at line 344; line 345 begins the `index_together` handling.

The check that decides whether RETURNING is kept is in `QuerySet._batched_insert` in `corpus/django/db/models/query.py`. It now reads `if bulk_return and (on_conflict is None or on_conflict == OnConflict.UPDATE):`. When that is true, `_insert` is called with `returning_fields=self.model._meta.db_returning_fields`. That keeps the RETURNING clause when `update_conflicts=True` (`OnConflict.UPDATE`). It still drops it for `ignore_conflicts=True` (`OnConflict.IGNORE`). I did not run anything, so this comes from reading the code only.

The code already contains this change. The original check was presumably just `on_conflict is None`, which the ticket describes as where the RETURNING part gets removed.

The `assert len(returned_columns) == len(objs_without_pk)` check in `bulk_create` (line 813–817) still applies only when `on_conflict is None`.

In the reverse one-to-one branch of get_related_selections, the code passes `related_select_mask` to `select_related_descend()`. It should pass the parent's `select_mask`. The forward-relation branch at line 1211 already does this. `select_related_descend` checks whether the field is in the mask it receives. The per-field mask doesn't contain the field, so `only()` is ignored for the reverse relation and all of the related model's columns get selected. I did not run any code or tests to confirm this.

The bug is in FunctionTypeSerializer.serialize in django/db/migrations/serializer.py. For a classmethod, it builds the path from `klass.__name__`. A nested class's `__name__` leaves out its outer class, so the migration gets the wrong default. It should use `klass.__qualname__` instead. I haven't applied or tested the change.
